liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): The band sounded locked in from the opening notes, and the magic lasted all show; Opened fuzzy, fast and booming, but a bit sloppy and overeager [19][22]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Patient and endearing, with Jerry playing lovely high notes [22]
- **He's Gone** (1 other source): Followed by a jam, then Drums, then another jam before I Will Take You Home [5]
- **Drums** (1 review): Watching the drummers from behind the stage was a spectacle [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Spoonful**: back after 128 archived shows (583 days) [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-04-12.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83768.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 147 min; rated 2.43/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd1989-04-12.149418.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 147 min [2]
- **gd1989-04-12.156414.OTS-Schoeps-PCM-Master-Mattes-Anon-Noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 153 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd89-04-12.sbd-matrix.willy.9962.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 140 min; rated 3.71/5 by 14 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the matrix sounds great, though the recording runs under two full discs; Clear, crisp sound with a good amount of audience noise; Slightly hissy in the highs, as expected from a cassette source [12][19][20][23]

## Around the show

- A 16-year-old borrowed his mom's station wagon; believing tickets were needed for the parking lot, they bought some [13]
- Reviewer sat second row between Jerry and Brent; Jerry laughed at him when he kept stepping away from the mic while photographing [17]
- Reviewer watched from behind the stage on Phil's side; hallway speakers existed and security was relaxed [21]
- Before the show, Phil sat alone in a chair backstage, smoking a joint [21]
- It was the reviewer's last show of the tour, having attended every one before it [23]
- Standards are well played for the year, but there is little jamming elsewhere [12]
- Reviewer ranks this among the top 10 of the 1989 shows, with Brent and the band on form [16]
- Reviewer rates it just behind the July 1989 Alpine Valley run, better than any other post-1981 show [19]
- Seen as the middle show of the three-night Rosemont stand, between the 11th and 13th [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-04-12.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83768.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [1]. Also: Cassette master from two Nakamichi 300/CP4 and two Sennheiser 441 mics, transferred to CD; taped by Walker and Scotton; Encore moved to the end of set one to fit two discs; second set and encore can be rejoined; Patch source was recorded by Steve Cherson [1]
- **gd1989-04-12.149418.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [2]. Also: Patch source supplied by Ted Mattes and Scott Clugston [2]
- **gd1989-04-12.156414.OTS-Schoeps-PCM-Master-Mattes-Anon-Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Master Audience PCM recording by Ted Mattes; transferred by Transfer by Anon Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel December 02, 2021; source: (OTS) Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics (ORTF) > Oade capacitor supply > Monster Cable ProLink > Sony pcm-f1 > Sony sl-2000 > PCM (Master) [4]
- **gd89-04-12.sbd-matrix.willy.9962.sbeok.shnf**: source: Ultramatrix (SBD/AUD mix)> Master Cassette> DAT> CD> SHN [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Liner Notes: [Grateful Dead Weekly #8: Rosemont Horizon – Rosemont, IL 4/12/89](https://linernotesmusicblog.wordpress.com/2016/04/14/grateful-dead-weekly-8-rosemont-horizon-rosemont-il-41289/) [25]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1989-04-12 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1989-04-12-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [26]
